candidate_sentence_map.S1: Nordecon’s financial performance weakened in 2025 despite a significant improvement in its order book.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Revenue declined 7% to €208.3 million from €223.9 million in 2024, mainly because Buildings segment revenue fell approximately 10% to €168.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Infrastructure revenue increased 10% to €39.9 million, supported by road construction, maintenance and Rail Baltica-related work.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Buildings still represented the majority of revenue at 81%, while Infrastructure accounted for 19%.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Gross profit decreased to €13.5 million from €16.8 million, and the gross margin fell to 6.5% from 7.5%.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Operating profit was €5.7 million, compared with €8.1 million in 2024, reducing the operating margin to 2.7% from 3.6%.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: EBITDA declined to €8.3 million from €11.0 million, while the EBITDA margin fell to 4.0% from 4.9%.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Administrative expenses decreased by approximately 14% to €6.8 million, primarily because weaker financial performance resulted in lower performance-based pay, but this reduction did not offset the decline in gross profit.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Net profit fell to €2.5 million from €5.2 million, and profit attributable to Nordecon’s owners decreased to €1.4 million from €3.8 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Earnings per share declined to €0.05 from €0.12.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Finance costs increased to €3.5 million from €3.0 million, mainly because the weakening of the Ukrainian hryvnia against the euro generated a €750 thousand foreign-exchange loss, compared with €258 thousand in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: In the fourth quarter, revenue rose to €60.6 million from €45.2 million, but gross margin fell to 5.9% from 9.0%, and the group recorded a €43 thousand net loss compared with a €618 thousand profit in the prior-year quarter.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: The construction market in Estonia stabilised during the second half of the year, although economic growth was modest at an estimated 1%, construction prices rose 1.5%, and competition remained intense.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Nordecon secured €235.0 million of new contracts, compared with €181.4 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Its order book reached €273.1 million at year-end, up 30%, with approximately 69% of the backlog scheduled for 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Infrastructure’s share rose to 42% from 18%, driven largely by major Rail Baltica and road contracts, while the Buildings backlog declined 7%.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Management expects business volumes to increase in 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Operating cash inflow was €1.2 million, while year-end cash declined to €5.3 million from €8.2 million, partly reflecting €2.9 million placed in long-term deposits.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Liquidity remained tight, with a current ratio of 0.93, and management identified liquidity exposure as higher than usual.

evaluation.label: Yes
evaluation.justification: All six key information units are adequately represented in the candidate summary. K1 is covered through multiple sentences detailing revenue decline, margin contractions, profit reductions, EPS drop, and the foreign exchange loss driver. K2 is fully covered with segment revenue changes and contribution percentages. K3 is represented with order book growth, Infrastructure segment driver, and 2026/2027-2028 scheduling. K4 is covered by cash flow details and long-term deposits. K5 is captured with liquidity metrics including current ratio and cash levels. K6 is addressed through stable employee count and staff cost reduction due to lower performance-based pay. No material omissions affect the overall understanding.
